subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw support distribution-backported shared SQLite through a persistent boolean bypass, or require an assertion tied to the exact detected SQLite build identity?
rationale: This defines a new operator configuration contract that can disable a database-corruption safeguard across upgrades; tests cannot determine the acceptable long-term safety policy.

options.title: Require exact-build assertion
options.body: Accept an override only when its configured value matches the runtime SQLite source or build identity, preventing a stale setting from authorizing a later unverified library.

options.title: Accept boolean override
options.body: Keep the proposed boolean escape hatch, but explicitly own the stale-upgrade risk and require strong documentation plus affected-image proof.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Do not add an override and require affected distributions to ship a recognized safe SQLite version or an OpenClaw-known verified build.

recommendation.title: Require exact-build assertion
recommendation.body: Accept an override only when its configured value matches the runtime SQLite source or build identity, preventing a stale setting from authorizing a later unverified library.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties vincentkoc to the adjacent installer-side WAL safety policy and version validation.
